Compare Existing Trial Planning Objects

Source: R/class_trial_comparison.R
getComparison.Rd

Creates a comparison of existing designs, design characteristics, sample size or power plans, and simulation results without recalculating them.

length() returns the number of objects in the comparison.

names() returns the supplied names of the comparison objects.

Usage

getComparison(..., objects = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'TrialComparison'
length(x)

# S3 method for class 'TrialComparison'
names(x)

Arguments

...

Designs, design characteristics, plans, simulations, lists thereof, or TrialComparison objects. Entries from ... precede entries from objects.

objects

Optional objects, lists of objects or TrialComparison objects. NULL is treated as an empty list.

x

A TrialComparison.

Value

An R6 TrialComparison inheriting from ParameterSet.

Details

The comparison retains references to its objects. Changes to an original object are reflected in subsequent comparisons; no comparison data are cached. $getObjects() and getObjects() return the named list of references. Replacing entries in that returned list does not change the comparison. length() is the number of objects and names() returns their supplied names (or NULL). Retrieve contained objects using comparison[[i]], comparison[["name"]] or comparison$name. R6 members take precedence for $; use [[ to retrieve an object whose name coincides with a member such as add. Unknown names return NULL. The fetch.TrialComparison() method provides the same object access through fetch(comparison, name) or fetch(comparison, position). Lists and comparisons are recursively expanded in their original order. Names on individual objects are retained; container names are discarded. Supplied non-empty names must be unique across the expanded collection; duplicate names raise an error. Unnamed entries and repeated references to the same object are allowed. getComparison() creates an empty comparison. Its data frame has zero rows and columns, and plotting requires numeric data to be added first.

comparison$add(..., objects = NULL) appends objects with the same input rules and returns the comparison invisibly, supporting chaining. All new entries are validated before the stored list is changed, including name collisions with existing objects. Adding another comparison copies its current list of references; subsequent additions to that source comparison do not affect the target. Existing summary objects remain snapshots; call summary() again after changing the collection.

comparison$delete(index) removes one object by its positive integer position or exact name and returns the comparison invisibly. Invalid positions or unknown names raise an error without changing the collection. Removing the last object leaves an empty comparison, which can be filled again. Names and order of remaining objects are retained; positions are renumbered. The S3 generics add() and delete() delegate to these methods and support pipelines such as comparison |> add(other) |> delete(1). Shallow cloning shares the contained objects. clone(deep = TRUE) is unsupported.

print() describes the collection and selected observed ranges. summary() groups differences by object scope, inputs/design settings and results, with equal profiles grouped by object number. Constants are compared independently of the number of rows. Nonconstant profiles retain stage/situation positions; repeated values across the other dimension are collapsed. Missing values and their positions participate in exact comparisons. No rounding or numerical tolerance is used to decide whether profiles differ.

Console and Markdown output are bounded. Limits and display rounding do not change the underlying data. as.data.frame.TrialComparison() returns the full comparison table. plot.TrialComparison() selects axes only when unambiguous. getObjectRCode() reconstructs the comparison and its contained objects; executing generated simulation code reruns the corresponding simulations.

Examples

comparison <- getComparison(list(
    fixed = getDesignFixed(), sequential = getDesignGroupSequential(kMax = 2)
))
print(comparison)
#> Design comparison
#> 
#> 2 objects; 3 comparison rows; 19 columns.
#> 
#> Object types:
#>     Fixed sample size design : 1
#>     Group sequential design  : 1
#> 
#> Observed metrics (across objects, stages and situations):
#>     Maximum number of stages : 1, 2
#>     Significance level       : 0.025
#>     Type II error rate       : 0.2
#> 
#> Available operations:
#>     summary(x)                                  : Compare differences
#>     as.data.frame(x)                            : Access all data
#>     plot(x, xParamName = ..., yParamName = ...) : Plot selected parameters
#>     getObjects(x)                               : Access contained objects
summary(comparison)
#> Design comparison summary
#> 
#> Comparison of 2 trial planning results: fixed sample size design, group sequential design.
#> The comparison identifies 10 differing parameters and 5 shared parameters or profiles.
#> Shared (examples): Endpoint, Calculation target, Significance level, Type II error rate, Test.
#> 
#> Object types and scope:
#> 
#>     Object type: character, factor [2 profiles]
#>         fixed: TrialDesignFixed
#>         sequential: TrialDesignGroupSequential
#> 
#> Inputs and design settings:
#> 
#>     Maximum number of stages: integer, factor [2 profiles]
#>         fixed: 1
#>         sequential: 2
#> 
#>     Type of design: character, factor [2 profiles]
#>         fixed: NA
#>         sequential: OF
#> 
#>     Binding futility: logical, factor [2 profiles]
#>         fixed: NA
#>         sequential: FALSE
#> 
#>     Tolerance: numeric, continuous [2 profiles]
#>         fixed: NA
#>         sequential: 1e-08
#> 
#> Results and derived parameters:
#> 
#>     Critical values: numeric, continuous [2 profiles]
#>         fixed: 1.959964
#>         sequential: [Stages = 1, 2] 2.796510, 1.977431
#> 
#>     Stage levels (one-sided): numeric, continuous [2 profiles]
#>         fixed: 0.025000000
#>         sequential: [Stages = 1, 2] 0.002582893, 0.023996469
#> 
#>     Information rates: numeric, continuous [2 profiles]
#>         fixed: NA
#>         sequential: [Stages = 1, 2] 0.5, 1.0
#> 
#>     Futility bounds (binding) / Futility bounds (non-binding): numeric, cont... [2 profiles]
#>         fixed (Futility bounds (binding)): NA
#>         sequential (Futility bounds (non-binding)): -Inf
#> 
#>     Cumulative alpha spending: numeric, continuous [2 profiles]
#>         fixed: NA
#>         sequential: [Stages = 1, 2] 0.002582893, 0.024999990
#> 
#> Legend:
#>     Profiles compare exact values at each stage and situation.
#>     NA: missing/unavailable.
#> 
#> Full data: as.data.frame(x). Exact profiles: summary(x)$parameterInfo.
head(as.data.frame(comparison))
#>   objectNumber                 objectType  endpoint calculationTarget
#> 1            1           TrialDesignFixed Undefined            Design
#> 2            2 TrialDesignGroupSequential Undefined            Design
#> 3            2 TrialDesignGroupSequential Undefined            Design
#>   objectName situation alpha beta sided criticalValues stageLevels kMax stages
#> 1      fixed         1 0.025  0.2     1       1.959964 0.025000000    1      1
#> 2 sequential         1 0.025  0.2     1       2.796510 0.002582893    2      1
#> 3 sequential         1 0.025  0.2     1       1.977431 0.023996469    2      2
#>   typeOfDesign informationRates futilityBounds bindingFutility tolerance
#> 1         <NA>               NA             NA              NA        NA
#> 2           OF              0.5           -Inf           FALSE     1e-08
#> 3           OF              1.0           -Inf           FALSE     1e-08
#>    alphaSpent
#> 1          NA
#> 2 0.002582893
#> 3 0.024999990
withCharacteristics <- getComparison(
    getDesignGroupSequential(kMax = 2),
    getDesignCharacteristics(getDesignGroupSequential(kMax = 3)))
combined <- getComparison(comparison, other = getDesignFixed(alpha = 0.05))
combined$add(list(getDesignFixed(alpha = 0.01)))
empty <- getComparison()
empty$add(getDesignFixed())
combined$delete(1)
combined$delete("sequential")
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot(comparison, xParamName = "objectNumber", yParamName = "criticalValues", plotLineEnabled = FALSE)
} # }
